questions.skill: Use relative frequencies in a two-way table to describe a possible association
questions.prompt: Is there evidence of an association between sleep and phone use at night? Explain using the row relative frequencies.
questions.prompt_markup: Is there evidence of an association between sleep and phone use at night? Explain using the row relative frequencies.
questions.correct_answer: Yes. 60% of those who sleep under 8 hours use a phone at night, but only 30% of those who sleep 8+ hours do.

sections.skill: Recognize conditional probability and independence in everyday situations

questions.domain: Statistics & Probability: Conditional Probability & the Rules of Probability
questions.skill: Recognize conditional probability and independence in everyday situations
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a first forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: Explain the difference between P(sleeps under 8 hours | uses a phone at night) and P(uses a phone at night | sleeps under 8 hours).
questions.prompt_markup: Explain the difference between P(sleeps under 8 hours | uses a phone at night) and P(uses a phone at night | sleeps under 8 hours).
questions.correct_answer: The first is the chance that a night phone user sleeps under 8 hours; the second is the chance that a person who sleeps under 8 hours uses a phone at night. The condition (the group you look in) is different.

questions.domain: Statistics & Probability: Conditional Probability & the Rules of Probability
questions.skill: Recognize conditional probability and independence in everyday situations
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a first forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: A fair coin is flipped twice, and the flips are independent. Is P(second flip is heads | first flip is heads) equal to P(second flip is heads)? Explain.
questions.prompt_markup:
A fair coin is flipped twice, and the flips are independent.
Is P(second flip is heads | first flip is heads) equal to P(second flip is heads)? Explain.
questions.correct_answer: Yes. Both are {1/2}; the first flip does not change the second.
